chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Ja'far from his father from their fathers, peace be upon them.

Imam Ali (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man who sold a commodity and stipulated two conditions: cash price thus and credit price thus, and he took the goods based on that condition, so he said: 'It is at the lower of the two prices and the longer of the two terms.' He means: He is entitled only to the lower of the two cash prices, extended to the credit term that was set.

key_terms.أَبْعَدِ الْأَجَلَيْنِ: The longer of the two terms
key_terms.أَقَلُّ الثَّمَنَيْنِ: The lower of the two prices

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling when a seller stipulates two different prices for cash and credit in a single sale?
ai.summary: This hadith from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *khiyar al-shart* (option of condition) in commercial transactions, where stipulating multiple prices grants the buyer the right to choose the lower price while retaining the benefit of the longer credit term. It reflects the practical jurisprudence of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) in resolving ambiguities in early Islamic trade, ensuring fairness by preventing sellers from arbitrarily selecting the higher price after the fact. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on contractual clarity and the protection of the buyer's interest in mixed cash-deferred sales.
